To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the study of protease activity during the senescing of cotyledon of Brassica napus is a promising experimental model; (ii) protease activities are associated with the senescence process in cotyledons; (iii) proteases involved in proteolysis during senescence are similar between cotyledons and leaves; and (iv) SA and ABA are involved in the induction of proteolysis during the senescense of cotyledons.

the protease machinery associated with efficient N mobilization during leaf senescing of Ténor genotype was also detected in cotyledons and that SA and ABA are involved in the regulation of proteolysis in cotyledons.
the senescence process of cotyledons of oilseed rape is characterized, as in senescing leaf of oilseed rape, by the induction of serine and cystein protease activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of proteolysis machinery in oilseed rape, a model crop species.
the regulation of proteolysis during leaf senescing of oilseed rape.
the study of the regulation of proteolysis machinery in oilseed rape.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
proteolysis in cotyledons during the senescing process is regulated in a similar way as in leaves.
protease activities are involved in the regulation of the senescence program in cotyledons of Brassica napus and are associated with the genotypic variability in nitrogen remobilization.
the proteolytic machinery is a promising target for improving nitrogen remobilization during leaf senescene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
protease activities are involved in the regulation of cotyledon senescence and that these activities may differ according to genotype and nitrate availability.
proteases involved in the nitrogen remobilization process are already present in cotyledons and that the infiltration of ABA or SA provokes an induction of the protease machinery.

proteolysis in cotyledons of oilseed rape is associated with the senescence process, and that protease activities in senescing oilseed rape cotyledons may be used as a model to investigate the genotypic variability in proteolysis associated to N remobilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteolysis machinery in senescing oilseed rape cotyledons is similar to the one in senescing leaf.
protease activities are correlated with the nitrogen remobilization in senescing tissues.
protease activities during leaf senescene are similar to the activities in cotyledon senescence.
